title: Arslanagić Bridge
visualBrief: The asymmetric pale-stone Trebišnjica crossing: two dominant pointed arches, a lower south water arch with a relief opening above it, three small south approach openings, a small north opening, raised stone parapets and a narrow double-crested cobbled walk.
nativeAxes: +X north-northeast toward the higher bank; -X south-southwest toward the longer low approach; +Z east-southeast. +Y up. Lowest source pier referenceY0; draft water referenceY1.2m.
sourceFacts: Retained catalog length80m; the current exact-QID OSM bridge outline measures85.14x4.162m including its mapped end extent. These extents remain distinct.
Three inspected ordinary2014 Diego Delso photographs show the asymmetric arch rhythm and the stacked south opening. Conflicting prose arch counts are not used as geometry evidence.

A consulted photo caption says6m height without a datum; no catalog height statement exists. Current opening rises and deck elevations are picture-based reconstruction assumptions, not a surveyed height claim.
Standard cached Protomaps20261020/Mapzen yields native water271.078674m; preliminary centerline banks are272.735939m at-X and276.717807m at+X.
reconstruction: Original analytic wall volume with genuine open arches, through-vault soffits, selected voussoir geometry and shared limestone, raw limestone and irregular stone paving surfaces. No downloaded meshes or photographic textures.
The working profile and opening dimensions are recorded in arslanagicControls. Three broad pier stubs interpret the visible buttress faces; their hidden/opposite-side construction is not surveyed.
No guardhouse is added: the inspected current exterior photographs show an open stone crossing.
